name: Monica AI
description: People who want one extension instead of five — writing, research, translation, and image generation in a single sidebar
pricing: Free (limited daily queries) / Pro $9.90/mo / Unlimited $19.90/mo
features:
• Context-aware sidebar that reads the current page before responding
• Multi-model support: GPT-4o, Claude, Gemini — switch freely
• Works inside any text field for inline writing assistance
• Image generation, translation, and summarization in one tool
• Clean, polished interface that doesn't feel like a side project
pros:
• Context-aware sidebar that reads the current page before responding
• Multi-model support: GPT-4o, Claude, Gemini — switch freely
• Works inside any text field for inline writing assistance

review:
Monica is the Swiss army knife of AI Chrome extensions. It floats as a sidebar on any webpage, and its key advantage is context awareness — it reads the page you're on before responding, so you don't have to copy-paste content into a separate chat window.

Generalists who work across many websites daily and want AI assistance everywhere without installing separate extensions for writing, research, and translation. If you already pay for ChatGPT Plus or Claude Pro, Monica might duplicate functionality — but if you don't, it's the single best extension to start with.

Sider's killer feature is group chat: send one prompt to multiple AI models at the same time and compare their responses side-by-side. This is genuinely useful for tasks where model quality varies — creative writing, code generation, nuanced analysis. Instead of guessing which model handles your prompt best, you see all the answers at once.

AI power users who already know the difference between models and want to pick the best answer for each task. Developers comparing code solutions, writers testing different creative approaches, analysts who want multiple perspectives before committing to an answer.

Power users who automate browser workflows, monitor competitors' pricing, or need to extract data from websites regularly. Also excellent for anyone with existing API keys who wants a free AI sidebar without a subscription.

Researchers, students, and content creators who need web-augmented AI answers. If your workflow involves reading lots of articles, watching educational YouTube videos, or analyzing documents, Merlin consolidates those research steps into one sidebar.

Sales teams scraping and enriching leads, marketers automating social media research, operations teams connecting browser workflows to business tools. Not for people who want a chat assistant — Bardeen is about automating actions, not answering questions.

Graduate students, research assistants, and professionals who read scientific papers as part of their job. If you regularly encounter papers with unfamiliar statistical methods, complex equations, or dense methodology sections, SciSpace turns a 2-hour read into a 30-minute one.

Heavy readers who want to build a personal knowledge base from web content. Content creators gathering research for articles, students building literature reviews, and anyone who highlights on Kindle and wishes they could do the same on the web.

review:

When you ask it to integrate a function, it runs the integration using Mathematica's symbolic computation engine. When ChatGPT integrates a function, it's pattern-matching against training data and sometimes gets it wrong. For advanced math, this distinction is critical.

The non-negotiable tool for college STEM students. If you're in engineering, physics, statistics, or any math-heavy program, Wolfram Alpha Pro is worth the $5/month (with student discount). review: iplan.ai does one thing well: it generates a complete multi-day itinerary in under 60 seconds. Tell it your destination, dates, interests, and budget, and it returns a day-by-day plan with activities, estimated times, and suggestions. It won't book your flights or optimize your driving route, but for travelers who just need a starting framework they can customize, it's the fastest path from "I have a trip" to "I have a plan."

For business travelers who take 20+ trips a year, that organization is worth more than any AI-generated restaurant list.

Developers on large teams or monorepos who hit context-window limits with other coding agents. The multi-agent architecture is genuine differentiation for enterprise-scale codebases, but if you're working solo on smaller projects, Claude Code or Codex will feel snappier. The contributor pricing is interesting for open-source developers who don't mind sharing data — you get Meta's infrastructure at a discount.

review:
On August 6, Google confirmed what had been rumored for months: starting September 4, 2026, Google Assistant will be replaced by Gemini on Android smartphones, Wear OS smartwatches, and compatible headphones. The rollout is progressive, but the direction is final — Google Assistant is dead.

Every Android user, whether they want it or not. The free tier is a direct upgrade over Google Assistant for most tasks — better at understanding complex questions, following multi-turn conversations, and handling ambiguous requests. Power users should look at AI Pro: at $19.99/mo, Gemini Spark turns your Google apps into a managed productivity system. The real impact won't be felt for months as the rollout stabilizes, but this is the moment AI went from "app you open" to "how your phone works."
